newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate closes flat after calm session.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate closes flat after calm session.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed unchanged at 29.50 percent on Monday, after a quiet session marked by light trade, dealers said.
"The U.S. bank holiday slowed trade down here. Rates barely moved and the peso was very stable," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed earlier 1.3 centavos firmer at 7.8950/7.8990.
U.S. banks were closed for Veterans' Day.

"We expect some upside pressure on rates tomorrow as there are forecasts that primary 28-day Cetes rates may gain a little at the auction, so most dealers will prefer to wait and see," the trader added.
Money market analysts forecast small gains for bellwether 28-day Cetes at the Banco de Mexico auction on Tuesday, and slight falls for longer term paper.
"We expect 28-day rates to fall only slightly, as although the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee is to meet soon, on Wednesday, we don't expect any chnage in U.S. rates," another trader said.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed 40 basis points down at 30.10 percent.
Banco de Mexico injected 3.765 billion pesos into the market, by assigning three credits at 31.24, 31.62 and 32.00 percent.

Total credit maturities for Tuesday were estimated at a hefty 8.509 billion pesos. Traders said the ensuing liquidity shortfall could be eased by government spending of about 2.5 billion pesos, however.
